title: Assam valley overview
description: The whole Brahmaputra valley in Assam, coarse. The basin-level view: where the river runs, where the hills close in, and how little vertical relief there is to work with.

encoding.note: code = round((elevation - offset) / step); no-data is code 0, and offset is one step below the lowest elevation so no real measurement can reach code 0

limitations: DSM, not a bare-earth DTM: buildings and vegetation are included, so slopes are surface slopes.
Water surfaces are flattened and rivers edited for consistency; there is NO riverbed bathymetry.
Vertical error LE90 is 1.472 m per source tile, a large fraction of the floodplain's few metres of relief.
Pixels are not square: GLO-30 is a 1 arcsecond grid, so ground size varies with latitude.

migration.change: every Terrain-RGB code incremented by 1 and encoding.offset reduced by one step, which is exactly invertible: (c+1)*step + (O-step) === c*step + O
migration.reason: the previous offset was the minimum elevation, so cells at that minimum encoded to code 0 and read back as no-data
migration.note: npm run data:dem was NOT re-run against this encoding. Byte-identical rebuild from source is therefore unverified; see docs/DATA.md section 13 and docs/ROADMAP.md phase 2.
